SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a Maasai red or blue checked cloth? (1 mark)
   A. Kikoi
   B. Shuka
   C. Kanga
   D. Uniform

2. Which houses in Lamu were built with coral stone? (1 mark)
   A. Boats
   B. Round grass houses
   C. Old town houses
   D. Tents

3. Which cloth is a printed cloth worn especially at the Kenyan coast? (1 mark)
   A. Jeans
   B. Shuka
   C. Kanga
   D. Suit

4. What should you do if you break a school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Run away
   B. Say sorry and accept fair guidance
   C. Blame others
   D. Hide it

5. What is the history of a school? (1 mark)
   A. The school timetable
   B. The school bell
   C. The school menu
   D. The story of how it started and changed

6. What are values? (1 mark)
   A. Types of buildings
   B. Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   C. Kinds of food
   D. Kinds of money

7. Which of these is a human resource? (1 mark)
   A. A lake
   B. A mineral
   C. A forest
   D. A skilled farmer

8. Which resource gives electric power from underground steam at Olkaria? (1 mark)
   A. Oil
   B. Wind
   C. Coal
   D. Geothermal heat

9. Which crop is grown mainly in sugarcane growing areas of Western Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Coffee
   B. Wheat
   C. Sugarcane
   D. Tea

10. Which of these is a benefit of industries? (1 mark)
   A. They close schools
   B. They remove roads
   C. They provide jobs
   D. They stop trade

11. What is a raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A machine
   B. A finished product
   C. A material used to make something new
   D. A worker

12. Which town is Kenya's main port and a busy industrial town? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Mombasa
   C. Kericho
   D. Nyeri

13. Why is teamwork important in a project? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the project fail
   B. It makes work harder
   C. It shares work and helps the project succeed
   D. It stops others helping

14. A group spent Ksh 400 and earned Ksh 700. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 700
   B. Ksh 1,100
   C. Ksh 300
   D. Ksh 400

15. Which colour is best for a road safety bib? (1 mark)
   A. Grey
   B. Bright orange or yellow
   C. Black
   D. Dark brown

16. You find a lost pencil that belongs to a classmate. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Keep it
   B. Sell it
   C. Return it to the owner
   D. Hide it

17. What is a role model? (1 mark)
   A. A person whose good behaviour others admire and copy
   B. A machine
   C. A kind of book
   D. A person who breaks rules

18. What does listening do for peace? (1 mark)
   A. It makes people angry
   B. It helps people to understand each other
   C. It wastes time
   D. It starts fights

19. What is the first step in solving a conflict peacefully? (1 mark)
   A. Hit
   B. Run away
   C. Shout
   D. Stop and calm down

20. Two pupils want the same ball. What is a peaceful solution? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Fight for it
   C. Take turns to play with it
   D. Break it

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain what peace means in a school. (2 marks)

22. Give three factors that promote peace in school. (3 marks)

23. Give two traditional foods and say where each is popular. (4 marks)

24. A group spent Ksh 900 and earned Ksh 600. Say whether this is a profit or a loss and find the amount. Suggest two reasons why it may have happened. (4 marks)

25. Match each activity to a resource it uses: fishing, farming, mining, tourism. (4 marks)

26. Name three natural resources found in Kenya and say how each is used. (3 marks)

27. Describe five actions that show good citizenship in school. (5 marks)

28. Explain how pollution can be reduced in an industry. (3 marks)

29. What does the Kiswahili word amani mean and why is it important in a school? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Shuka
   The shuka is a checked cloth worn by the Maasai.

2. C — Old town houses
   Old Lamu houses used coral stone.

3. C — Kanga
   The kanga is printed cloth popular on the coast.

4. B — Say sorry and accept fair guidance
   We should be honest and accept correction.

5. D — The story of how it started and changed
   History tells how the school began and grew.

6. B — Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   Values guide how we behave.

7. D — A skilled farmer
   People's skills and labour are human resources.

8. D — Geothermal heat
   Olkaria makes electricity from geothermal steam.

9. C — Sugarcane
   Sugarcane is grown in parts of Western Kenya.

10. C — They provide jobs
   Industries employ people.

11. C — A material used to make something new
   Raw materials are used to make products.

12. B — Mombasa
   Mombasa is Kenya's main port.

13. C — It shares work and helps the project succeed
   Sharing roles makes work easier.

14. C — Ksh 300
   700 - 400 = 300.

15. B — Bright orange or yellow
   Bright colours are easy to see.

16. C — Return it to the owner
   Returning shows honesty.

17. A — A person whose good behaviour others admire and copy
   Role models set good examples.

18. B — It helps people to understand each other
   Listening helps solve conflicts.

19. D — Stop and calm down
   We must calm down before talking.

20. C — Take turns to play with it
   Taking turns is fair.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Peace means pupils and teachers live together safely, respect each other and settle disagreements without fighting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for safety and respect, 1 mark for solving conflict peacefully.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Respect, sharing and forgiveness. Accept honesty, listening or fairness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: githeri in central Kenya and fish with ugali near Lake Victoria. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food and 1 mark for each correct place.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: It is a loss of Ksh 300. Sales may have been low because the price was too high or not enough people knew about the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for loss, 1 mark for the amount 900 - 600 = 300, 1 mark for each reason.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fishing uses lakes or ocean, farming uses land and soil, mining uses minerals, tourism uses wildlife or beaches.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is used for drinking and farming. Land is used for farming and grazing. Minerals such as soda ash are used in factories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each resource with a use.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Arrive on time, keep the compound clean, respect teachers, share with others, and report bullying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each action.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Treat waste before releasing it, plant trees, and use clean machines or methods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Amani means peace. It is important because pupils feel safe and can learn well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 mark for the reason.
